History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
26-year-old man with known asthma presents via telehealth with 3 hours of chest tightness, mild dyspnea, wheeze, and non-productive cough following an upper-respiratory tract infection; ran out of his preventer and reliever inhalers last week.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Chest tightness for 3 hours.  
• Timeline:  
  – Had a cold last week (sore throat, runny nose, general malaise); URI symptoms improving except cough.  
  – Chest tightness and mild shortness of breath began ~3 hours before consult and persist.  
• Character: Tight sensation rather than pain; feels unable to achieve full breath. Non-productive cough, wheeze.  
• Severity/functional impact: Not breathless at rest but more winded than usual when climbing stairs.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: No inhaler use in past week (ran out); no specific relieving factors reported.  
• Associated symptoms: No chest pain, no productive sputum, no fever mentioned.  
• Pertinent ROS negatives (elicited): No ear pain, no current significant runny nose; denies chest pain.  
• Prior similar episodes: Severe asthma exacerbation age 16–17 requiring intubation and several-day hospitalization; otherwise stable for years with regular inhaler use.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – on Salbutamol (Ventolin) PRN and Clenil Modulite (inhaled steroid) maintenance; both out of supply for one week.  
• Allergic rhinitis/hay fever.  
• Dust allergy (environmental).  
• Childhood eczema (resolved).  
• Childhood milk-protein allergy (resolved).

Medications:
• Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; none available currently.  
• Clenil Modulite (beclomethasone) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; none available currently.  
• No other regular medicines reported.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies (NKDA).  
• Non-drug allergies: dust.

Social History:
• University student; was away at university last week.  
• Smoking: not discussed.  
• Alcohol/recreational drugs: not discussed.  
• Employment: not specified; doctor advised possible sick leave.

Family History:
• Mother – eczema.  
• Father – asthma.

Physical Examination:
(No in-person exam performed; telehealth visit)  
• Vitals: not obtained.  
• General appearance reported only through history; patient able to converse in full sentences, no rest dyspnea.

Investigations:
• None performed or available during consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation likely triggered by recent upper-respiratory infection and lapse in preventative therapy.  
  – Prescribe Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler.  
  – Prescribe Clenil Modulite (inhaled corticosteroid) for maintenance.  
  – Provide spacer device with instructions.  
  – Educate patient: use Ventolin PRN; if requiring Ventolin more often than every 3 hours or if symptoms worsen (increasing SOB, chest tightness, light-headedness), seek urgent medical attention.

Issue 2: Current exacerbation requiring systemic corticosteroids.  
  – Prescribe oral steroid course: two tablets each morning for 5 days (exact drug/dose not documented in transcript).  
  – Review potential side effects (mood change, hyperglycemia, rash, nausea, headache); advise to read pharmacy leaflet.

Issue 3: Medication non-adherence / supply lapse.  
  – Arrange prescriptions to be sent within the hour.  
  – Reinforce importance of continued daily inhaled steroid use.  
  – Encourage keeping inhalers available when away from home/university.

General plan items:  
  – Advise rest; patient may self-certify sick leave for up to 7 days as needed.  
  – Safety-netting provided: attend ED or call emergency services if deterioration occurs.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: vitals, physical exam findings, complete medication doses/routes/frequencies, smoking/alcohol history.  
• Internal conflicts: none noted.  
• Transcript quality: minor audio dropouts but overall intelligible; no apparent data loss.
